newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares in broad market slide on U.S. woes.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares in broad market slide on U.S. woes.

text.p: Swedish shares began the week on a dour note as rate-sensitives were hit by a bout of nerves ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve meeting on Tuesday. A fall in Wall Street on opening did little to bolster sentiment.

The all-share index closed 1.26 percent lower at 2,016.21 in turnover of three billion crowns. Banking was the only index not to close lower as rumours of merger talks between S-E-Banken and Handelsbanken fuelled a sharp rise in these shares early on.
Although the banks concerned declined comment on the newspaper report that gave rise to the merger speculation, S-E-Banken rose 0.50 crowns to 59.50 kr and Handelsbanken rose one crown to 155.50.
Market focus has returned to Wall Street and to the Federal reserve, which meets on Tuesday.
Brokers said an increase of 25 basis points in key U.S. rates is discounted in Swedish share prices, but warned that a higher increase could wreak havoc on the market.

The day's worst-performing index was investment, which closed 2.1 percent lower. Investor shed four crowns to 241, and brokers said the stock was hit by a downturn in drugs group Astra, which also closed four lower at 271.
Investor owns a large stake in Astra.
Ericsson was also dragged down by market woes, losing 2.50 crowns to 163.50.
